title: Slain man's name surfaced in B.C. court; Oakville Shooting: [National Edition]
article: The 38-year-old man fatally shot by police in an Oakville park over the weekend in a possible suicide-by-cop died of multiple gunshot wounds, autopsy results revealed yesterday.

But authorities in Ontario and British Columbia could not confirm whether the dead man, Steve Remian, was the same person whose name surfaced at the Robert "Willie" Pickton trial -- where a jury is now deliberating on the fate of the Port Coquitlam pig farmer in the slayings of six of the women who went missing from Vancouver's notorious Downtown Eastside.

DNA belonging to a Steve Remian was discovered on a blanket along with that of Mr. Pickton and one of the alleged victims. The name Steve J. Remian was also found on the label of a suitcase in Mr. Pickton's workshop. The evidence was mentioned at the year-long trial -- though it is important to emphasize Mr. Remian was not a suspect.

The man who was shot by Halton Regional Police in southeast Oakville's Wedgewood Park at 2:33 a.m. on Saturday was driving a vehicle with B.C. plates and was reported to have recently returned from the West Coast.

Neither the Special Investigations Unit probing the Oakville shooting nor the RCMP's Missing Women's Joint Task Force in B.C. would confirm they were the same Steve Remian. The coincidence has nevertheless ignited speculation about the timing of the two events.

"All I can say about him right now is that he had B.C. plates on his car, and that he was an Oakville resident who had moved to B.C. and that he had come back to Ontario," said Rose Bliss a spokeswoman for the SIU. "We don't have any confirmatory information to indicate whether or not it is the same person, and it's really not our job or our priority at this stage to determine whether or not there is a connection between the two.... As the investigation develops and we get further information, all of his personal information will be factored into the totality of what we have."'

Constable Annie Linteau, an RCMP spokeswoman for the missing women task force, said it had received no request for information in relation to the dead man and she was unable to comment further at this sensitive juncture in the Pickton case with jury deliberations under way.

Mr. Pickton has been on trial in the killings of Mona Wilson, Sereena Abotsway, Marnie Frey, Brenda Wolfe, Andrea Joesbury and Georgina Papin but still faces charges for the murders of 20 other women.
Halton Police responded to a 911 call at 1:34 a.m. on Saturday about a man who was behaving strangely and carrying a gun at a Tim Hortons on Oakville's Trafalgar Road.
By the time officers arrived the man had fled, but a description of the vehicle was radioed to all cars on patrol.

About 45 minutes later, at 2:17 a.m., a cruiser intercepted the suspect vehicle and pursued it, accompanied by a second patrol car, to nearby Wedgewood Park in a tony neighbourhood in the southeast corner of the bedroom community.
After a brief confrontation, three of four responding police officers fired multiple shots and Mr. Remian died of his injuries.

"Our investigators did recover a rifle from the shooting scene and that is going to be examined," Ms. Bliss said. "Those officers have been designated as subject officers and ... their guns and uniforms have been taken for examination as well as all the other physical evidence that was found at the scene."
Friends of the dead man expressed disbelief that the Steve Remian downed by police bullets was the person they remembered as retaining his "optimism" despite a troubled family life in his youth.

"It was quite a shock," said Michael Clifford, who was a couple of years ahead of Mr. Remian in high school in Oakville. "Steve wasn't that kind of guy. It was not like him to be confrontational in any way.
"Steve was always a very kind, considerate, sweet guy, always thinking of others."

The two recently reconnected through the social-networking site Facebook, where Mr. Clifford, of Vancouver, learned Mr. Remian had found a new job in Ontario repairing vehicles. "He liked working with his hands, he liked building," he said.
Through other Facebook friends, a portrait has emerged of an individual who moved frequently around the country.
Ivan Langdon said he knew Mr. Remian briefly when the two worked on the site of the Snap Lake diamond mine in the Northwest Territories operated by De Beers.

"I was a co-worker of Steve's for about eight months," Mr. Langdon recounted in an e-mail. "Steve worked underground driving a fuel truck. Outside of work, I knew very little about him or his family."
Some of the other members of the dead man's clique of 21 Facebook friends also said they didn't know much about Mr. Remian's past.
One woman, who did not want her name used, memorialized him with an inscription on the top of her Facebook page: "R.I.P Steve u will be missed and loved always :'(."
British Columbia court records reveal that a Steven Joseph Remian was embroiled in divorce proceedings in Penticton between 1994 and 1996.
Steve Remian, age 38, also posted a profile on the movie review site Flixster, using the handle starvingwolf and listing his place of origin as "end to end Canada."
He said his favourite films were "Lord of the Rings, Natural Born Killers and Hero." He cited Johnny Depp and Winona Ryder as his favourite actors, but decorated his site with photos of Liv Tyler.
